chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the solemn oath (Ila'): When a man takes an oath that he will not approach his wife, nor touch her, nor join his head with her head, he is in a period of grace as long as four months do not pass. When four months have passed, he is paused (given a choice): either he fulfills (the oath by returning), so he touches her, or he is determined upon divorce, so he separates from her until she menstruates and becomes pure from her menstruation, then he divorces her with one divorce before he sleeps with her, with the testimony of two just witnesses. Then he is more rightful in reverting to her as long as the three pure periods (Quroo') do not pass.

key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Solemn oath of abstention from wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and procedure for Ila' (solemn oath of abstention) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the procedural mechanics of Ila', emphasizing the husband's four-month grace period before being compelled to choose between resuming intimacy or initiating divorce. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that the final divorce occurs after one menstrual cycle, preserving the husband's right of revocation (Raj'ah) during the three subsequent pure periods, a structure designed to balance marital stability with the resolution of prolonged abstention.
